purpose: Normal and Challenge trainer source. Both modes keep the same level caps; Challenge adds one readable interaction, a bounded roster delta, and sharper AI.

knobs.boss_level_offsets: Per-member offsets from each configured ace.
knobs.member_counts: Length of each boss members array and route archetype member_count.
knobs.ai: ai_profiles values; maxSelectMargin must stay positive.
knobs.route_density: Route placements arrays; ordinary coordinates must remain route-polyline vertices, while explicit off-route trainers must record and validate their route anchor and gap.

normal.intent: Readable first solution, limited item pressure, and one mechanic at a time.

challenge.intent: Same cap and answer classes; one extra interaction or threshold, never a hard-counter pile.

placements.name: Trail Novice
placements.lesson: Introduces trainer sight lines, accuracy changes, and priority without threatening the first-route team.

dialogue_text.pre: First battle? Mine too. If our eyes meet on the road, we battle—ready?
dialogue_text.player_win: Sand Attack bought me a turn, but it could not fix a bad matchup.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Quick Attack closes a fight before nerves can.

placements.name: Meadow Apiarist
placements.lesson: Uses two gentle Bug-area species to teach switching and accessible Flying or Electric answers.

dialogue_text.pre: The Combee followed the flowers; Surskit followed the water. I learned to pack answers for both.
dialogue_text.player_win: You switched instead of forcing one partner through everything. That is the lesson.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Bug teams look gentle until you let them control the field.

placements.name: Vale Naturalist
placements.lesson: Uses two fast wetland species to reinforce Water as a Brock answer without pretending the dry River of Shrews vale contains a fishable river.

dialogue_text.pre: This vale holds water after every storm, even if the old river never did.
dialogue_text.player_win: You changed targets before Quick Attack could pin you down. Brock will not wait either.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Fast Water types turn a dry path into their own ground.

placements.name: Plateau Guide
placements.lesson: A bulky opener followed by Grass and Water pressure is the final rehearsal for Brock.

dialogue_text.pre: Brock survives the obvious first hit. Bring a second answer for what comes after.
dialogue_text.player_win: That is a team ready for stone: pressure from more than one direction.
dialogue_text.player_loss: One counter is a plan. Two counters are a team.

normal.intent: Learn roles, switching, and preserving two answers for Brock.

challenge.intent: Same lesson with one berry threshold and an extra member only on the final rehearsal.

placements.name: Ravine Scrapper
placements.lesson: Shows that setup and recovery can be denied and that the resulting opening should be used immediately.

dialogue_text.pre: Corphish does not need a long plan. It denies yours and takes the opening.
dialogue_text.player_win: You attacked before Taunt stole your setup. Good.
dialogue_text.player_loss: You gave Corphish time, and it took all of it.

placements.name: Glowbug Keeper
placements.lesson: Status, stat control, and recovery show how low damage becomes dangerous when tempo is lost.

dialogue_text.pre: The lake's glowbugs do not hit hard. They make sure you never hit cleanly.
dialogue_text.player_win: You broke the cycle before Charm, confusion, and Moonlight piled up.
dialogue_text.player_loss: A weak attack matters when the other side controls every turn.

placements.name: North Bank Angler
placements.lesson: Rewards shoreline exploration and teaches that physical Water pressure and high physical Defence call for Grass or special Electric attacks before Misty.

dialogue_text.pre: Most people see Viltri from the south road and think they have seen the lake. The north bank disagrees.
dialogue_text.player_win: Krabby pushes hard and Shellder closes up. You changed the kind of pressure instead of repeating it.
dialogue_text.player_loss: The bank rewards a long walk, but it still expects the right answer.

placements.name: Lake Surveyor
placements.lesson: Rain, speed control, and a Water/Grass core rehearse Misty and show why Electric alone is incomplete.

dialogue_text.pre: Rain changes this whole shore. Did you bring one answer, or two?
dialogue_text.player_win: Electric pressure handles open water. Flying or Bug pressure handles what grows in it.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Misty's lake will not give you one clean weakness to chase.

normal.intent: Learn denial, recovery pressure, and separate Electric and Grass plans.

challenge.intent: Sharper move choice and one extra final-rehearsal member; no rain lock or coverage trap.

placements.name: Climbing Novice
placements.lesson: Rock Tomb demonstrates speed control and Howl presents a visible setup turn to punish.

dialogue_text.pre: On a climb, controlling the footing matters more than moving first.
dialogue_text.player_win: You punished Howl before Rock Tomb could keep you slow.
dialogue_text.player_loss: One speed drop was enough to decide the slope.

placements.name: Grove Ranger
placements.lesson: Complementary Fighting and Flying/Psychic pressure teaches that one resistance is not a switching plan.

dialogue_text.pre: The grove punishes teams built around one resistance. Show me your second switch.
dialogue_text.player_win: You saw the partner behind the first matchup.
dialogue_text.player_loss: One safe switch led straight into the other threat.

placements.name: Groundkeeper
placements.lesson: Bunnelby demonstrates Ground damage while Skiddo demonstrates the Electric-resistant fallback.

dialogue_text.pre: Burrows and roots both carry current into the earth. That is how you face Surge.
dialogue_text.player_win: You found the opening before Ground and Grass could settle in.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Bunnelby can grow into your clean Ground answer. Skiddo is the fallback when Ground gets disrupted.

placements.name: Signal Watcher
placements.lesson: Paralysis and control preview Surge's tempo while the dialogue names Ground, Grass, and priority as answers.

dialogue_text.pre: That mast keeps changing the way everything moves. Let us see how your team handles lost tempo.
dialogue_text.player_win: Good. Do not race Surge—use Ground, Grass, or priority to take the turn back.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Paralysis makes speed unreliable. Bring an immunity or a way to act first anyway.

placements.name: Vessu Ranger
placements.lesson: A Ground immunity, action denial, and an Electric-resistant recovery user form the final Surge rehearsal.

dialogue_text.pre: The mountain's safest teams redirect electricity instead of trying to endure it.
dialogue_text.player_win: You brought immunity, resistance, and pressure. That is enough to challenge the shelf.
dialogue_text.player_loss: The pond behind you offers Wooper. Bunnelby stays on the critical path. Use one of them.

normal.intent: Learn Ground immunity, resistance, priority, and recovery after lost tempo.

challenge.intent: A single status-curing berry and fuller rehearsal teams, without hidden Ground counters.

player_team_snapshots.fairness: Multiple common Water/Grass answers; players can still bring neutral utility.
Electric and Grass families are both present before the lake gym.
One dependable immunity core exists; a second broad Ground family is missing.
Independent Flying, Ice and Fire lines exist.
Split Electric/Psychic/Ground offense answers Koga's immunity coverage.
One ambient Dark/Steel/Bug plan exists; mansion Ghosts remain optional and unproven.
Water, Ground and Rock answers are independently established.
Availability is broad, but fairness cannot be judged until Giovanni's format and roster are decided.
